Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (6)
Grrr...

The exploded fragment's unleashed spirit and Sun energy surged wildly. The lightning energy of the surrounding Battle Kings, forming a giant semicircle around the battlefield, was gradually pushed back by its force.
Ban slowly regulated her breathing.

Although she had overwhelmed Nirgand in the battle, she was not without damage. Especially the deep wound inflicted by the golden horn towards the end, even for Ban, required a sufficient recovery period.
If she hadn't felt Siron's energy approaching, Ban would have taken a brief moment to stabilize her energy before supporting her brothers.
"Brothers, hang in there a bit longer. Reinforcements are coming soon."
Ban's low voice traveled across the blackened grounds, reaching her dispersed brothers.
'Reinforcements?'
'Do we have reinforcements? I thought our brothers were waiting at the entrance to the Black Sea.'
'Could she be referring to those expedition friends!?'

Then, Ban sat down in a meditative posture and calmly entered meditation. As the Heart of Light and lightning energy were refined, spheres of lightning energy appeared across the battlefield like lanterns.

The spirit and Sun energy pouring from the fragment seemed reluctant to invade Ban's area, as if scared beasts fleeing. The energy from the fragment was directed solely towards the lightning energy of the Battle Kings.
'Just containing the energy left by that dead guy is so strenuous, how did Brother Battle God manage to capture it alone, and in such a short time…'
The Battle Kings, once again astonished by Ban's martial prowess, vigorously pulled together their lightning energy.
About twenty minutes later, the Battle Kings felt the spirit and Sun energy diminishing, thanks to the reinforcements Ban mentioned.
A vast and unapproachable energy was shaking the depths of the Black Sea, distinct from Ban's.
Despite being pushed back from the battlefield by Nirgand's aftermath, the Battle Kings distinctly felt that energy.
'Siron Runkandel, Jin's father…!'
They shivered down their spines.
The existence of someone like Ban, the pinnacle above Genesis, made the Battle Kings involuntarily open their mouths in awe.
'I expected as much when Brother Battle God said he wanted to cross swords with her, but to this extent?'
The feeling was like the sea or the sky itself moving closer, an overwhelming presence. The spirit and Sun energy, trying to spread outward, were lost under the pressure of Siron and Ban's energies.
The brothers calmed their astonishment and closed the encirclement again. They eagerly wanted to return to the battlefield and see Jin's father in person.
Of course, they moved while thoroughly sealing off any remaining spirit and Sun energy, ensuring not a speck escaped.
Another ten minutes passed. When they arrived at the battlefield where Nirgand was subdued, the brothers saw two giants facing each other.
Amidst the floating blue spheres, Ban sat in meditation, and Siron stood quietly, watching her.
Siron did not pay any attention to the newly arrived Battle Kings, not out of disregard, but to avoid disturbing Ban's meditation.
A moment later, the Battle Kings quietly took their positions, understanding his intention.
Looking around the two people and their surroundings, the Battle Kings wondered if this place could still be called the Black Sea.
The lightning energies of Ban, brilliant enough to appear sacred, seamlessly mixed with Siron's white energies.
The battlefield, illuminated by the combined powers of the two giants, shone peacefully like a temple.
Nirgand's corpse had completely vanished, and the fragment of the Sun God he harbored floated between them, gently vibrating.
“…Sorry to have kept you waiting, Siron Runkandel.”
Soon after, Ban opened her eyes and stood up.
"It's alright. You took care of quite a troublesome nuisance for me, so it's no big deal. You must be the brother of the youngest, the Battle God of the Plutonian."
"Yes, I'm Ban. I've heard a lot about you from Brother Jin, and now we meet like this."
"I haven’t heard much about you. Apparently, I wasn’t a great father."
"No need to feel too embarrassed. Brother Jin doesn’t resent you."
Both smiled simultaneously.
"These are my brothers, Baba, Baltirok, and Kaio."
"Pleased to meet you, Siron."
"Likewise."
A little behind Siron, Ozdok crouched down. He was quite surprised and annoyed by a group of beastmen speaking rudely to Siron, but he was too scared to intervene.
Swoosh!
[Egad!]
Suddenly, when Siron drew his sword, Ozdok was startled and fell on his butt.
It was a shocking moment. Instinctively, he felt that even Siron could not be safe if he fought that person.
Meanwhile, the Battle Kings' faces lit up with excitement, eager for the encounter.
"May I ask for a match?"
Ban nodded eagerly, as if she had been waiting for it.
"Of course. However, as you can see, I'm not in my best condition, so I worry if you might be disappointed."
"Haha, spending time with the youngest seems to have influenced you. Making such modest remarks, uncharacteristic of you."
"Is it that obvious?"
"Well, the youngest and we are of different sorts, after all."
Ban also drew her sword, Sigmund. She naturally gave Siron the first move, and he accepted her gesture smoothly.

For Siron, this was a very fresh experience. Since reaching the realm of 10 stars, he had never had the opportunity to make the first move in any duel. Back in his youth, those who dared offer him the first move out of arrogance all ended up beheaded with a single strike.
"Will one move really be enough, Siron?"
"Unfortunately, we both have our duties, so it can't be helped. Then, I’ll make my move."
Siron closed the distance to Ban in a sliding motion, not too fast. Given their realm, the mere ten steps between them were insignificant.
Barisada descended vertically, and Sigmund rose horizontally.
There was no dazzling technique, no incredible speed typical of superhumans, or the transcendent brute strength of giants.
It was literally just a single exchange of moves, yet both found this duel more exciting than any they had experienced before.
Clang...!
The two blades clashed, producing a sharp metallic sound. It was the pure sound of steel meeting steel, unenhanced by lightning energy or aura.
The two swords remained stuck together for a while, completely still.
It was a kind of power struggle. Although their expressions didn't change, both started to radiate heat from their bodies before even 5 seconds passed.
Ozdok couldn't understand what was happening, and the Battle Kings watched, not even blinking, as they swallowed dryly.
It was merely one exchange, but to the Battle Kings, it seemed like a match of the century. To anyone at a similar level, it would have appeared that way.
'This is insane!'
'Is, is Brother Battle God being pushed back a bit...!?'
'Unbelievable.'
The Battle Kings kept swallowing dryly. There were only very subtle changes, but Barisada was gradually pushing back Sigmund.
Both were breathing heavily, but it seemed more strenuous for Ban. Naturally, the Battle Kings, who had never imagined Ban being pushed back by anyone, struggled to believe what they were seeing.
'Indeed, Master is amazing...!'
Ozdok wanted to applaud and cheer for Siron, but he felt he might be killed by the Battle Kings if he did.
This was a new feeling for Ozdok, too. The sensation of potentially being killed by someone other than Siron.
Just two finger widths.
Shortly after Barisada pushed back Sigmund by that much, Ban and Siron simultaneously withdrew their swords. The Battle Kings gasped, and Ozdok screamed internally.
Siron and Ban, both drenched in sweat, seemed unsatisfied.
"Siron, you won."
"Ha, making strange remarks again?"
"What's the problem?"
"I had two hands, and you had one. And all I did was push back by two finger widths."
"That’s true. And just for the record, I'm not in my best condition."
"Ah... right, that's true. But come to think of it, at our level, whether it’s one hand or two doesn’t really matter."
"Hmm, is that so? Anyway, congratulations, Siron. You are the only being who has achieved a victory against me."
Silence followed for a while. The Battle Kings, who had been in shock, felt relieved, and Ozdok became somewhat annoyed, though he couldn't dare utter a word.
"Brothers, if you have any jewel wine, bring it here."

The Battle Kings quickly brought out the jewel wine and handed it to Ban. Siron, suppressing his rising frustration, Siron neatly adjusted the fallen sleeve, untied the armor on his shoulder, and roughly wiped the inside with his hand.
Then, he handed the slightly dirtier armor to Ban. She hesitated for a moment before accepting it reluctantly.
"Most humans don’t like it, but I thought you might appreciate the taste even without a Heart of Light."
"Just give it to me."
Gulp gulp gulp...
Clear jewel wine filled the armor. Clang, their armor clashed, and both emptied their drink in one go.
"Excellent liquor."
"If I knew we would meet like this, I would have brought proper food and drink. Luna said that food is precious to the expedition, so take this with you."
"Alright. Are you leaving now?"
"Yes. Do you need my help? Only that Morganil remains now, right?"
"He's someone only I can catch. But on my way here, I found an odd trail. It seems to be a dimensional gate used by those who empowered Nirgand."
Ban's eyes widened.
"Ho... a dimensional gate of the Sun God Religion. That means my brothers and I might have one less troublesome matter to deal with."
"It seemed Nirgand left it intentionally. It looks like he was used by them."
"Could you guide me there?"
"Of course."
"Then let's go right a...”
Ban suddenly staggered. Siron naturally caught her. The Battle Kings were once again alarmed and rushed to Ban's side.
"That's why you should have used both hands. Showing off your pride against me, and now look at the embarrassment."
Ban’s anger flared up at the comment, but she sighed and nodded.
"True, I regret it now. But what can I do? In the same situation, you would have done the same."
"Hm, that's true. Let me know when you’re ready, and I’ll guide you to that dimensional gate."
